result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use gateways to control divergence and convergence, never to represent work. Identify exclusive, inclusive, parallel, event-driven or complex behavior.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description lists several activities performed by one actor in a comma-separated sequence, states no ordering or dependency among them, and then a later activity is described as following all of them: Model the listed activities as parallel branches: fork them from the preceding step with a parallel gateway, and join them with a parallel gateway before the later activity, so the later activity waits for all branches. Do not chain the unordered activities in a fixed sequence unless the description states an order.

When the description names several activities that must all be finished before the process moves on or ends, and it gives no order among them: Model a parallel gateway that splits into those activities as concurrent branches, and a second parallel gateway that joins the branches before the next element or the end event. Do not chain the activities in a fixed sequence, and do not join them with an exclusive gateway.

When the description names several activities that must all be finished before a later activity can start, and it states no decision or order among them: Model the named activities as parallel branches opened by a parallel gateway, and join them with a parallel gateway before the later activity. Use an exclusive gateway only when the description states a choice between the activities.

When the description states that an ongoing activity continues while, once a checkpoint or milestone is reached, another activity is started, and the two are described as running at the same time with no order or choice between them: Model a parallel gateway at the point where the checkpoint is reached. Give it one outgoing branch for the continuing activity and one for the newly started activity, both unconditional. Do not place an exclusive gateway or a decision condition on these concurrent branches, and do not sequence the continuing activity after the new one.
